title: Infinitely many prime losing positions in subtract-a-square
credit: QED original (archived Nov 2026, restored after re-review).
plain: In subtract-a-square, players alternately remove a positive square number of tokens from a pile, and whoever cannot move loses. Show that infinitely many prime pile sizes are losing positions for the player to move.
math: Let $\mathcal P\subset\mathbb N_0$ be the P-positions of subtract-a-square: $0\in\mathcal P$, and $n\in\mathcal P$ iff $n-k^2\notin\mathcal P$ for all $1\le k\le\sqrt n$. Prove that $\mathcal P$ contains infinitely many primes.
